# Requirements Quality Checklist: The Mobile Menu Takes the Header's Theme

**Purpose**: Review the requirements for quality before implementation — clarity, completeness,
consistency, modifiability, traceability and scope — not the implementation itself.
**Created**: 2026-10-16
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [tasks.md](../tasks.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Clarity

- [ ] CHK001 Does the specification say which surface is the reference — the header's *displayed treatment*, read from `overDark`, rather than a colour guessed at the call site?
- [ ] CHK002 Is "the navbar's background" resolved to a single mechanism before any requirement uses it, rather than left to the reader to infer from three treatments?
- [ ] CHK003 Does FR-004 name the three selectors explicitly, so "compatible interaction" cannot be read as "whatever the author felt like"?
- [ ] CHK004 Is the touch case explained rather than implied — is it stated *why* `:focus-visible` cannot carry it on iOS?

## Completeness

- [ ] CHK005 Are all three of the header's treatments accounted for — black, transparent and scrolled-white — rather than only the two the request names?
- [ ] CHK006 Is the call to action covered, given that it renders through a different style than the navigation items?
- [ ] CHK007 Is the entrance animation covered as a flash source, given that its current start colour is white?
- [ ] CHK008 Are the requirements that must NOT change stated as requirements — the header's appearance, the portal target, the focus behaviour?

## Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 Does any requirement contradict the constitution's styling rule, or introduce a mechanism beside styled-components rather than within it?
- [ ] CHK010 Do the two accents in FR-005 match the two `specs/022` measured, rather than being restated with different values?
- [ ] CHK011 Does the specification agree with the plan about which declarations of the mobile link change — both, or one?
- [ ] CHK012 Is there any place where the specification describes the mechanism and the plan describes a different one?

## Modifiability

- [ ] CHK013 Is the theme a single shared fragment, so that changing the palette is one edit rather than a search?
- [ ] CHK014 Does the feature add exactly one prop, so the cost of moving the portal later is known and bounded?
- [ ] CHK015 Could the interaction colour be changed without touching the component that renders the item?

## Traceability

- [ ] CHK016 Does every functional requirement have at least one task that implements it, and does every task name a file?
- [ ] CHK017 Is every success criterion measurable from a rendered page or from the source, rather than from an opinion about appearance?
- [ ] CHK018 Is each criterion honest about whether it is measured in a browser, computed as arithmetic, or read from the source?
- [ ] CHK019 Is every criterion actually checkable by someone who did not write it? A criterion that needs a reviewer to know which files count as "a second write" is not checkable, and neither is one whose exclusions live in prose elsewhere.
- [ ] CHK020 Does every requirement that forbids a change say how that preservation is verified, rather than leaving it to good intentions?

## YAGNI

- [ ] CHK019 Is anything present that the request did not ask for and that can be deleted without losing a requirement?
- [ ] CHK020 Is a new token, a new component or a new dependency proposed that an existing one already covers?
- [ ] CHK021 Does the specification avoid fixing things it merely noticed, such as the focus trap that is a no-op today?

## Notes

- **Nothing here is marked.** This checklist has been written, not reviewed; every marker is the
  reviewer's to set, and none of them says anything about whether the feature works.
- **CHK018 is the one worth spending time on.** `specs/022` drew the same line and stated it plainly:
  nothing is asserted about how the result looks, and no screenshot is compared. If a future reviewer
  finds a criterion here that cannot be measured, that criterion is the one to cut.
- **The review found that SC-005 had claimed a ring the menu does not have.** `Navigation.styles.ts`
  declares no `:focus-visible` at all, so only the close button and the call to action draw an outline.
  The criterion was rewritten to name both mechanisms and the gap, and the gap is recorded in all three
  documents rather than smoothed over.
- **CHK019 and CHK020 exist because this review found two gaps.** SC-006 originally read "none of the
  nine override values is written a second time anywhere under `src/`", which four assertions in
  `Header.test.tsx` already violate on purpose — the criterion was uncheckable until it named its
  exclusions. And FR-009 and FR-010 forbid changes, which is a claim about absence, so the plan and the
  tasks now say what verifies them instead of leaving it implied.
- **CHK021 protects the scope.** The broken focus trap in `useMobileMenu.ts` is real, pre-existing, and
  deliberately out of scope. A reviewer who wants it in should say so before Phase 3, not after.
